title: A Simple and Rapid Agarose Gel Electrophoresis Method to Assess CpG Methylation of DNA
author: Marco Paliza-Carre

steps.title: Prepare restriction digest reactions
steps.instruction: In 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, add DNA (1 µg per 50 µL reaction), 10 µL of 6× TriTrack DNA loading dye, and 3.16 µL of 10 % SDS; add any other reagents required for the enzyme as listed.

steps.title: Incubate and spin digest
steps.instruction: Incubate the reactions in a 37 °C water bath for 1 hour, then briefly centrifuge in a microcentrifuge at up to 8000 rpm (≈6000 g).

steps.title: Prepare agarose gel and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.5 cm‑thick 1.5 % agarose gel in 1× TAE, make 900 mL of 1× TAE running buffer, and prepare a staining solution of 1× SYBR Safe in 150 mL 1× TAE.

steps.title: Load samples and ladders
steps.instruction: Load 100 ng of each DNA sample (or 300 ng of GeneRuler 1 kb+ ladder) into 3 mm‑wide × 1.5 mm‑deep wells, placing ladder lanes on both sides of the sample lanes.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 100 V (≈6.7 V cm⁻¹) for 100 minutes.

steps.title: Stain gel
steps.instruction: Cover the gel to protect from light and stain in the SYBR Safe solution for 1 hour on a shaker set to 150 rpm.

steps.title: Image gel under blue light
steps.instruction: Verify that none of the bands intended for analysis are oversaturated, then capture an image with a blue‑light gel documentation system using a 400‑ms exposure (adjust if needed for a different system).

steps.title: Open gel image in TotalLab
steps.instruction: Launch TotalLab CLIQS software and open the saved gel image file.

steps.title: Create analysis protocol with settings
steps.instruction: Generate a new analysis protocol and set: check “Invert Image Intensity”, Rolling Ball = 200, Minimum = 1, Noise reduction = 5, %Max Peak = 1, “Maximum peak of the:” (as shown), Gel Edges = Automatic Detection.

steps.title: Select area of interest and run analysis
steps.instruction: On the image, draw a minimal area of interest (AOI) that encloses all ladder and sample bands, then run the protocol you just created.

steps.title: Verify lane and band detection
steps.instruction: Confirm that lanes have been generated accurately and that each band is correctly defined.

steps.title: Configure Rf calibration
steps.instruction: Open the “Rf Calibration” tab, select “keep Rf lines aligned with no lane”, deselect “Use curved Rf lines”, enable “Snap Rf lines to Bands when dragging”, drag points from the 0 Rf line to the top 20 000 bp ladder band and from the 1 Rf line to the bottom 75 bp ladder band, delete any extra points, and ensure the top line reads 0.000 and the bottom line reads 1.000.

steps.title: Export measurements to clipboard
steps.instruction: At the top of the window choose Export → Export to Clipboard → Measurements Table.

steps.title: Calculate mRf in Excel
steps.instruction: Paste the exported table into Microsoft Excel and compute mRf using the provided formula (Rf₁ = Rf of band 1, V₁ = raw volume of band 1, n = number of bands detected in the lane).

steps.title: Identify intermediate bands and compute ratio
steps.instruction: For the pSV40‑sGAD55‑BLa sample, define intermediate bands as those between 4 880 bp and 700 bp (excluding the 4 880 bp and 700 bp bands). Use Excel to calculate the intermediate/total ratio with the given formula.
